marta: Heads-up — I’m seeing a reproducible p99 regression on mixed-precision routes after the continuous-batcher scheduler change. Only on workloads with small KV stripes (kvstripe=8/16).
lee: Can you drop the perf summary / small repro?
marta: Quick numbers from ci-infer (same config, three runs):
```
model: redwood-mosaic-7b
runner: ci-infer-rt01
batcher: continuous-v2
kvstripe: 16
quant profile: fp8 primary, int4 fallback
baseline p99 (master@before): 78ms
current p99 (after scheduler tweak): 92ms  (+18%)
throughput  tokens/s: baseline 4200 -> now 3700 (-12%)
kernel selection log: fp8_block_pack -> FALLBACK int4_tile_copy
padding waste ratio: baseline 9% -> now 28%
```
marta: The interesting bit is kernel swap: the selector seems to prefer an fp8 kernel for the shape, but runtime ends up copying/padding to int4 tile shape which creates extra memcpy and prologue cost.
lee: That padding jump to 28% is huge. Do you have a kernel-swap trace?
marta: Pasting a trimmed trace (stack style) — timestamps are ms since request start:
```
0   continuous-batcher: received request shape [1, 512]
2   scheduler: assigned to pool A (kvstripe=16)
4   kernel-selector: candidate fp8_block_pack(shape=16x64) score 0.87
6   runtime: kvcache-shard mismatch -> remap to int4_tile(shape=8x128)
7   runtime: allocate pad buffer + tile-copy (memcpy 1.2ms)
10  kernel launch int4_tile -> execution 3.4ms
```
marta: So the selector picks fp8 but later a KV remap forces a different physical tile layout; overhead is the copy + extra padding.
anup: This matches something I saw in telemetry last week — the scheduler started preferring pool A for latency SLOs which has different slab stride. Might be a placement/stripe incompatibility.
sara: Could quant calibration impact this? If the fp8 kernel had slightly worse numeric score we fall back to int4 and then copy?
lee: The trace shows selector favored fp8 initially (score 0.87). The fallback happens because runtime detects 'kvstripe mismatch'. So it isn't numeric fallback, it's shape/layout mismatch.
anup: Agreed. Two potential fixes: (1) make selector aware of kvstripe/pool layout (avoid picks that will be remapped) or (2) add a lightweight in-place tile converter kernel to avoid memcpy penalties.
marta: I ran a quick microbench: in-place tile-converter reduces extra latency from ~1.2ms memcpy+0.6ms prep down to ~0.3ms, nets ~0.9ms saving on p99. That would restore ~10% of the regression on this workload.
sara: What about padding waste — can batching heuristics avoid creating the pad-heavy shapes?
anup: continuous-batcher mispredicted the modal shape because of the scheduler's prefetch window. For small KV stripes we get many single-seq requests that push the batcher to pad to uncommon tile dims. We should tune the batcher’s shape-prior or use shape-aware slit.
lee: For immediate triage: can we (a) add a telemetry flag to log "selector->remap" events, (b) run a bisect on the scheduler PR that changed placement heuristics, (c) prototype the tile-converter kernel?
marta: I opened a quick repro run script: `./tools/run_infer --model mosaic-7b --quant fp8,int4 --batcher continuous --kvstripe=16 --repro 1000` — it reproduces locally.
anup: I'll add the selector->remap telemetry and a telemetry dashboard tile. Will also run the scheduler PR bisect tomorrow.
sara: I'll try the in-place converter microkernel and post perf. If it looks good we can land as a hotfix to reduce p99 while we fix selector logic.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026.3.14 succeeded in pool-A earlier (no errors). :white_check_mark:
lee: Cool — assign owners? Marta (repro + smoke), Anup (telemetry + bisect), Sara (converter prototype). I'll coordinate a follow-up in #eng-runtime tomorrow.
marta: Added issue #4857 with logs and the trace, tagging @anup @sara and linking the repro. I'll paste a short flamegraph in the issue.
anup: One more note — if we change selector to consider kvstripe, run a config sweep because it might cause different tail behavior on large-batch workloads. Might need a gating flag behind runtime config.
sara: Agreed. I'll prototype converter behind a feature flag first.
marta: Thanks — will keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
